scenario.title: QA methods: choosing the kind of proof
situations: The user asks how a behavior will be verified.
A change needs deterministic assertions, visual judgment or exploratory investigation.
An existing suite runs locally or through declared CI.
scenario.current: Research trace; requirements and source paths need live proof.
questions: Built-in method definitions and current skill/doc consumers were read; Pack methods and live registry availability are delegated to the QA-machine owner.
Command nodes, when present, were checked with installed CLI --help only; this proves parser/help availability, not serving-control-plane capability or successful execution.

lessons.title: Choose proof before choosing machinery
lessons.when: When defining acceptance evidence or binding an existing test suite for the first useful change.
lessons.need: A method defines the runner, capability needs, evidence and verdict path. Cases select methods; instructions alone do not create a runner.
lessons.surface: QA Methods tab; method list/get; test setup and requirement intake
lessons.gap: The clearest method introduction is non-public. Review question: should FIRST-USER publish that small explanation with one current first-work example?

lessons.title: Distinguish check, inspection and exploration
lessons.when: When the expected outcome requires assertions, visual judgment or exploratory observation.
lessons.need: Command/CI and Browser check use automatic results; Browser inspection captures evidence for agent judgment. Pack-added methods and exploratory missions have additional contracts. A screenshot is not a pass.
lessons.surface: Method definitions; Browser reference; exploratory QA dispatch
lessons.gap: Review question: should verification planning offer the relevant method in plain language and fetch its reference only after selection?
